text: Temperatures begin dropping across Texas. Grid operators issue a weather watch. Natural gas plants are running normally, wind is moderate.
Arctic blast arrives. Temps plunge below 0°F in parts of the Panhandle. Demand starts climbing as heating load increases. Gas prices begin spiking.
Heating demand pushes ERCOT load above 65 GW. Natural gas wellheads and processing plants start freezing. Some wind turbines ice up in West Texas.
Gas supply disruptions cascade. Plants that depend on just-in-time gas delivery begin tripping offline. Instrument air lines freeze at coal plants.
ERCOT enters Energy Emergency Alert (EEA) Level 1. Over 10 GW of generation is offline. Operating reserves plummet. Voluntary conservation appeals issued.

At 1:25 AM, ERCOT orders transmission operators to shed load. Over 30 GW of generation offline — nearly half the grid. 4.5 million customers lose power. The grid comes within minutes of total collapse.
Blackouts continue for millions. Some areas have been without power for 24+ hours. Water systems fail as pumping stations lose electricity. Gas supply remains critically constrained.
Temperatures stabilize. Some generators begin coming back online. ERCOT starts restoring load in stages, but millions remain without power.
Demand drops as temperatures moderate slightly. More generators return. Load shedding decreases. Most customers regain power, though some areas remain dark.
Grid returns to normal operations. Final load shed ends. The human toll: an estimated 246 deaths, $195 billion in damage, and fundamental questions about grid resilience.
